(a) There must be a separate throttle control for each engine.
(b) Throttle controls must be grouped and arranged to allow--
  (1) Separate control of each engine; and
  (2) Simultaneous control of all engines.
(c) Each throttle control must provide a positive and immediately responsive means of controlling its engine.

(a) There must be a separate throttle control for each engine.
(b) Throttle controls must be grouped and arranged to allow--
  (1) Separate control of each engine; and
  (2) Simultaneous control of all engines.
(c) Each throttle control must provide a positive and immediately responsive means of controlling its engine.
[(d) If a power or thrust control incorporates a fuel shutoff feature, the control must have a means to prevent the inadvertent movement of the control into the shutoff position. The means must--
  (1) Have a positive lock or stop at the idle position; and
  (2) Require a separate and distinct operation to place the control in the shutoff position.]
